diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that from now on we assume periodic boundary conditions. For this reason we set
It is orthonormal, i.e. $\mathbf E\mathbf E^H = \mathbf E^H\mathbf E = \mathbf I$

issues.failure_explanation: For "periodic" boundary conditions the stencils must be circulant with wrap-around entries. The text instead zeroes the first and last rows of D^x and the neighbouring entries of D^{xx}, which gives homogeneous Dirichlet-type matrices. For these matrices the antisymmetry of D^x fails. Take y=e_{N_x-1} and z=e_{N_x}: y^T D^x z = 1/(2Δx) but z^T D^x y = 0. The identity with D^+ also needs a periodic D^+_{N_x,1}, which is not defined. The Fourier matrix E diagonalises only circulant matrices, and with Δx=1/N_x the functions exp(iαπx_j) are not orthonormal. So the lemma's hypotheses do not match the stated definitions.

failure_location.quote: \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^x z_i = - \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} y_i

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define D^x, D^{xx}, D^+ as circulant matrices with the wrap-around entries (D^x_{1,N_x}=-1/(2Δx), D^x_{N_x,1}=+1/(2Δx), etc.). Take Δx = L/N_x with a consistent Fourier phase, e.g. exp(2πiαx_j/L).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the matrices used in the schemes do not satisfy the properties that the CFL lemma and both stability proofs rely on.
issues.title: Stencil matrices as defined are not periodic, so the summation-by-parts lemma (and Fourier diagonalisation) fails as stated
issues.why_classification: The intended periodic circulant structure is clear and the fix is a local redefinition; all conclusions and the CFL constant survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for $g_{jk}^n = 1$ the condition $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} g_{jk}^n \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$ holds
which are equal to $1$ up to order $\mathcal{O}\left(10^{-3}\right)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs (1/√(2π)) Σ_k ω_k e^{v_k²/2} = 1 exactly. This is not a hypothesis of the lemma, and it is not an identity of Gauss-Hermite quadrature. The integrand e^{v²/2} is not a polynomial, so the rule is not exact for it. The paper itself reports deviations of order 1e-3 in the 2D example. Without the identity, Σ_k f_{jk} ω_k e^{v_k²} = ρ_j is not preserved. The cancellation of the σ-term in the stability proof, Σ_k M(M−f)ω_k e^{3v_k²/2}=0, relies on the same identity.

failure_location.quote: We insert the induction assumption as well as $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the normalisation as a hypothesis, or renormalise the weights (e.g. rescale ω_k so that (1/√(2π))Σω_k e^{v_k²/2}=1), and note that the scheme then uses the modified quadrature.
issues.overall_effect: The moment property and the σ-term cancellation in both stability theorems hold only if the quadrature normalisation is assumed or enforced. This is not established for the Gauss-Hermite weights actually used.
issues.title: Moment-preservation lemma uses an unstated, generally false Gauss-Hermite normalisation identity
issues.why_classification: Adding or enforcing a scalar quadrature normalisation is a short local fix that leaves the method, proofs, and CFL result intact.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs (ρ^{n+1})² g^{n+1}_{·β} to lie in span(X̿), and ω e^{v²/2} ⊙ g^{n+1}_{j·} to lie in span(V̿). The augmentation only adds (ρ^{n+1})² X̂ and ω e^{v²/2} V̂ to the span. The S-step output g^{n+1}=X̿ S̿ V̿ᵀ is the Galerkin projection onto the full 4r-dimensional span. Its columns in general have components along both X̂ and (ρ^{n+1})² X̂. Multiplication by (ρ^{n+1})² then produces components along (ρ^{n+1})⁴ X̂, which is not in the span. The same holds in velocity. So the displayed identities, and the step that removes the projections P^X, P^V, do not follow from the augmentation.

failure_location.quote: We now use the fact that we have augmented the bases in \eqref{alg:KbasisAug} and \eqref{alg:LbasisAug}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified. At minimum, a repair must give a Galerkin construction in which the test function (ρ^{n+1})² g^{n+1} (and its velocity analogue) provably lies in the projection space. One option is a projection that is orthogonal in the 𝓗-weighted inner product, with correspondingly redefined bases and a redone proof.
issues.overall_effect: The central claim of an analytical stability proof with a CFL condition for the low-rank scheme is unsupported. The practical rank-2r scheme used in all 2D experiments has no stability argument at all.
issues.title: DLRA stability proof: basis augmentation does not give the claimed range identities
issues.why_classification: The stability guarantee for the DLRA scheme is the paper's main theoretical claim, and the only argument for it rests on a false inference. Any fix needs a new construction or proof architecture, not a local patch.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a prescribed tolerance parameter $\vartheta$ the new rank $r_1 \leq 2r$ is chosen such that

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate is derived for the pre-truncation S-step output X̿ S̿ V̿ᵀ. The scheme's output f^{n+1} is the truncated factorisation. Truncation discards singular values of size up to ϑ and changes g^{n+1}. The truncation is a Frobenius-norm projection of g, whereas the stability norm weights f = ρ g e^{-v²/2} by ρ_j² and ω_k e^{3v_k²/2}. Nothing shows that the truncated 𝓗-norm does not exceed the untruncated one. The claim that truncation "does not alter these expressions" is therefore unsupported. In addition, the moment-preserving construction assumes X̿ S̿ V̿ᵀ Z = 1 before truncation. The Galerkin S-step, which solves only the projected equation, is never shown to preserve this moment. That moment is needed for the σ-term cancellation inherited from the full-order proof.

failure_location.quote: as the truncation step is designed not to alter these expressions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove that the (moment-preserving) truncation is non-expansive in the 𝓗-norm, e.g. by truncating in the weighted inner product. Alternatively, state the weaker result ‖f^{n+1}‖_𝓗² ≤ ‖f^n‖_𝓗² + O(ϑ). Also prove that the S-step preserves the moment constraint.
issues.overall_effect: Monotonic decay ‖f^{n+1}‖_𝓗 ≤ ‖f^n‖_𝓗 is not established for the actual (truncated) low-rank scheme. At most it holds up to a truncation perturbation, which is not quantified.
issues.title: DLRA stability proof ignores the truncation step and the unproven moment constraint
issues.why_classification: The gap is contained in the truncation step: a weighted truncation or a perturbed statement gives a comparable result without redoing the Galerkin/CFL argument, but it is more than a routine fix.
